paragraphs.source_en: Dear Sir, at this season of autumn chill, I respectfully offer congratulations on the continued prosperity of your household. I beg to state that, as you are aware, this school has since the year before last been obstructed by two or three ambitious persons, and though matters once reached an extreme, I have privately concluded that all this arose from the unworthiness and want of virtue of myself, Shinsaku, and I take it deeply to heart as a warning. Thereafter, through my own sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall, and after enduring every hardship, I have at last gradually contrived, by my own strength alone, a way to obtain funds for the building of an ideal new schoolhouse. In brief, I propose to publish a volume entitled Special Number: An Outline of the Secrets of Western Dressmaking; this book is truly the fruit of many years of painstaking research by myself, Shinsaku, written according to the principles and laws of industrial art, without sparing my very heart's blood. Now, in order to spread it among households at large, I respectfully ask that it be purchased freely, with only a slight profit added to the cost of printing. I venture to think that, if this can be done, it will on the one hand aid the development of this art, and on the other the slight profit thereby gained may be applied to the cost of constructing the schoolhouse. Accordingly, though I feel most deeply ashamed, I humbly beg you, in the interest of this school's building fund, to show generous support by purchasing one copy of the Outline of Secrets presented here, or by bestowing it upon one of the maids of your household, thereby displaying the noble virtue of your approval; should you graciously consent, I shall be boundlessly grateful. Respectfully yours.

paragraphs.source_en: My master coldly crumpled this solemn letter into a ball and tossed it with a plop into the wastepaper basket. Poor fellow: all Mr. Shinsaku's laborious nine bows and all his sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall came to nothing. My master then took up the third letter. This letter, however, shone with a most novel brilliance. The envelope was printed in a red-and-white checkered pattern, quite like the signboard of a candy seller, and in the middle of this gaudy cover, in thick clerical script, were written the words: To Mr. Chino Kushami, beneath the Tiger's Banner. One could not guarantee whether some Miss Ota would come out of it, but at any rate the outside of the letter was exceedingly splendid. The letter read as follows:

paragraphs.source_zh: 主人冷淡地将这封郑重的来信搓了个团儿，砰地丢进了字纸篓里。可怜，那针作先生费尽力气的九拜，针作先生的卧薪尝胆，都没起任何作用。主人又拿起第三封信。这封信却以它的新奇而大放异彩。信封是用红白两色格子印成的，活像卖糖块的图案，在这色彩醒目的封皮当中，用浓重的隶书体写着：“珍野苦沙弥先生虎帐下”几个字。虽无法预知信中会不会出现“多多样”，反正这信的外表是够漂亮的了。信是这样写的：

paragraphs.source_en: If I regulate Heaven and Earth by myself, I could drain the waters of the Western River in a single gulp; if Heaven and Earth regulate me, then I am merely dust upon a strange road. One must say: what connection, after all, is there between Heaven and Earth and myself? ... The first man to eat sea cucumber deserves reverence for his courage of spirit; the first man to eat blowfish deserves honor for his bravery. He who ate sea cucumber was Shinran returned to this world; he who ate blowfish was an incarnation of Nichiren. As for Mr. Kushami, he knows only dried gourd strips in vinegar-miso. I have never yet seen a man who could eat dried gourd in vinegar-miso and be a gentleman of the realm.

units.source_en: If I regulate Heaven and Earth by myself, I could drain the waters of the Western River in a single gulp;
units.source_zh: 若以我律天地，则可一口吸尽西江水；

units.source_en: if Heaven and Earth regulate me, then I am merely dust upon a strange road.
units.source_zh: 若以天地律我，则我仅为陌生尘而已。

units.source_en: One must say: what connection, after all, is there between Heaven and Earth and myself?
units.source_zh: 须道：天地与我，究有什么关涉？

units.source_en: ... The first man to eat sea cucumber deserves reverence for his courage of spirit;
units.source_zh: ……首次食海参者，应敬佩其胆力；

units.source_en: the first man to eat blowfish deserves honor for his bravery.
units.source_zh: 首次食河豚者，应尊重其勇气。

units.source_en: He who ate sea cucumber was Shinran returned to this world; he who ate blowfish was an incarnation of Nichiren.
units.source_zh: 食海参者乃亲鸾之再来，食河豚者乃日莲之转世。

units.source_en: As for Mr. Kushami, he knows only dried gourd strips in vinegar-miso.
units.source_zh: 至如苦沙弥先生，则只知醋腌干瓢而已。

units.source_en: I have never yet seen a man who could eat dried gourd in vinegar-miso and be a gentleman of the realm.
units.source_zh: 食醋腌干瓢而能为天下之士者，吾未之见也。

paragraphs.source_zh: 若以我律天地，则可一口吸尽西江水；若以天地律我，则我仅为陌生尘而已。须道：天地与我，究有什么关涉？……首次食海参者，应敬佩其胆力；首次食河豚者，应尊重其勇气。食海参者乃亲鸾之再来，食河豚者乃日莲之转世。至如苦沙弥先生，则只知醋腌干瓢而已。食醋腌干瓢而能为天下之士者，吾未之见也。

paragraphs.source_en: Your intimate friend shall sell you for his own advancement; your parents shall have their partialities against you; the person you love shall abandon you and go away. Wealth and rank are by nature hard to rely on; office and stipend shall be lost in a single morning. The learning secretly stored in your head shall grow mold; what, then, do you intend to rely upon? Within Heaven and Earth, what is there to depend on? God?

units.source_en: Your intimate friend shall sell you for his own advancement; your parents shall have their partialities against you; the person you love shall abandon you and go away.
units.source_zh: 密友将卖汝以求荣，父母将私于汝，汝所爱之人，将弃汝而去。

units.source_en: Wealth and rank are by nature hard to rely on; office and stipend shall be lost in a single morning.
units.source_zh: 富贵原难保，爵禄将一朝而失去。

units.source_en: The learning secretly stored in your head shall grow mold; what, then, do you intend to rely upon?
units.source_zh: 汝头中秘藏之学问也将生霉，汝何所恃乎？

units.source_en: Within Heaven and Earth, what is there to depend on?
units.source_zh: 天地之间何所依凭乎？

units.source_en: God?
units.source_zh: 神？

paragraphs.source_zh: 密友将卖汝以求荣，父母将私于汝，汝所爱之人，将弃汝而去。富贵原难保，爵禄将一朝而失去。汝头中秘藏之学问也将生霉，汝何所恃乎？天地之间何所依凭乎？神？

paragraphs.source_en: God is nothing but an earthen doll fabricated by man in the extremity of suffering. Man is nothing but a stinking carcass congealed from excrement that had to be discharged. To rely on what must not be relied upon and call it peace: tut, tut! A drunken man idly toys with wild words and staggers toward the graveyard. When the oil is spent, the lamp goes out of itself; when karma is exhausted, what can remain? Mr. Kushami, pray sit down and have some tea!

units.source_en: God is nothing but an earthen doll fabricated by man in the extremity of suffering.
units.source_zh: 神无非为人痛苦之极捏造之土偶而已。

units.source_en: Man is nothing but a stinking carcass congealed from excrement that had to be discharged.
units.source_zh: 人，无非为不得不排泄之粪便所凝结之臭皮囊而已。

units.source_en: To rely on what must not be relied upon and call it peace: tut, tut!
units.source_zh: 恃不足恃谓之求安，咄咄！

units.source_en: A drunken man idly toys with wild words and staggers toward the graveyard.
units.source_zh: 醉汉漫弄胡言乱语，蹒跚走向坟场。

units.source_en: When the oil is spent, the lamp goes out of itself; when karma is exhausted, what can remain?
units.source_zh: 油尽而灯自灭，宿业尽，则何物可遗？

units.source_en: Mr. Kushami, pray sit down and have some tea!
units.source_zh: 苦沙弥先生且坐吃茶！

paragraphs.source_zh: 神无非为人痛苦之极捏造之土偶而已。人，无非为不得不排泄之粪便所凝结之臭皮囊而已。恃不足恃谓之求安，咄咄！醉汉漫弄胡言乱语，蹒跚走向坟场。油尽而灯自灭，宿业尽，则何物可遗？苦沙弥先生且坐吃茶！

paragraphs.source_en: If one does not regard others as human beings, there is nothing to fear; but what of such a person, who does not regard others as human, becoming indignant at a world that does not regard him as himself? It is just as men of power, rank, and success have gained their position by not regarding men as men. Yet when others do not regard them as themselves, they flush with anger. Make whatever face you please, you fool!

units.source_en: If one does not regard others as human beings, there is nothing to fear; but what of such a person, who does not regard others as human, becoming indignant at a world that does not regard him as himself?
units.source_zh: 不以他人为人，则无所畏惧，不以他人为人者，愤激于此种不以我为我之人世，则又当如何？

units.source_en: It is just as men of power, rank, and success have gained their position by not regarding men as men.
units.source_zh: 正如权贵荣达之士得以不以人为人也。

units.source_en: Yet when others do not regard them as themselves, they flush with anger.
units.source_zh: 至于当他人不以我为我之时，则怫然作色。

units.source_en: Make whatever face you please, you fool!
units.source_zh: 任君作色可矣，混蛋！

paragraphs.source_zh: 不以他人为人，则无所畏惧，不以他人为人者，愤激于此种不以我为我之人世，则又当如何？正如权贵荣达之士得以不以人为人也。至于当他人不以我为我之时，则怫然作色。任君作色可矣，混蛋！

paragraphs.source_en: When I do not regard others as human, or when others do not regard me as myself, the malcontent descends from heaven in a fit. This convulsive activity is called revolution; revolution is not the doing of malcontents, but what men of power, rank, and success deliberately bring into being. There is much ginseng in Korea; sir, why do you not take it?

units.source_en: When I do not regard others as human, or when others do not regard me as myself, the malcontent descends from heaven in a fit.
units.source_zh: 我之不以他人为人时，或人之不以我为我时，不平家则抽风式自天而降。

units.source_en: This convulsive activity is called revolution; revolution is not the doing of malcontents, but what men of power, rank, and success deliberately bring into being.
units.source_zh: 这种抽风式活动，名之曰革命，革命并非不平家之所为，乃权贵荣达之士有意使之产生者也。

units.source_en: There is much ginseng in Korea; sir, why do you not take it?
units.source_zh: 在朝鲜，人参极多，先生为何而不服用之？

paragraphs.source_zh: 我之不以他人为人时，或人之不以我为我时，不平家则抽风式自天而降。这种抽风式活动，名之曰革命，革命并非不平家之所为，乃权贵荣达之士有意使之产生者也。在朝鲜，人参极多，先生为何而不服用之？
